title: Tinder: How messaging can be disastrous
description: This is a light-hearted talk on how dating apps like Tinder provide messaging guarantees to it's users. Every time a user sends a message on chat, Tinder avoids disaster with three important features:  1) Guaranteed Delivery A user can be sure of their message eventually reaching the recipient if the server has received the message. Achieved using retrials of failed messages.  2) Ordered Delivery The messages are sent to the recipient in the same order that the server received them.  3) Idempotency If a failed message is retried, and there are duplicate messages received on the client, the client displays only of the duplicate messages.   P.S: Try to find a better pick up line than the one mentioned. This is an example of 'Tinder Fail', after all :P And the two memes in the video have the text: "This is why...I don't use Tinder" "LOLOLOL...Can I have your number?"  Technical Details: https://youtu.be/WzBzYX1aSrU  References:  https://doc.akka.io/docs/akka/2.2.4/general/message-delivery-guarantees.html http://www.enterpriseintegrationpatterns.com/patterns/messaging/GuaranteedMessaging.html https://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/en/SSLTBW_2.1.0/com.ibm.zos.v2r1.ieai600/ieai635.htm https://stackoverflow.com/questions/21363302/rabbitmq-message-order-of-delivery https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idempotence http://www.restapitutorial.com/lessons/idempotency.html  DISCLAIMER: I am pretty sure that Tinder provides all of the messaging guarantees we wanted in the video. This video is not describing how their system (does/doesn't) work.
